description: Create all templates for the Kitchen Staff interface: a minimal base_kitchen.html layout with a stripped-down sidebar (no Order Management, Dashboard, Finance, etc.), and the kitchen/orders.html order-card page with realtime SSE JS. Also add test coverage. Depends on FEAT-001 and FEAT-002.
steps: 1. Create templates/base_kitchen.html extending templates/base.html. Structure mirrors base_admin.html but drastically simplified sidebar. The sidebar contains ONLY: brand header ('Kape De Manubag' + ☕ logo), a nav section with a single link to {% url 'kitchen:orders' %} using Lucide icon 'chef-hat' (or 'utensils' if chef-hat is unavailable in lucide 0.469.0 — check the version loaded in base.html: unpkg.com/lucide@0.469.0). Label: 'Kitchen Orders'. At the bottom of the sidebar: the user avatar/name block (same as base_admin.html .sidebar-user pattern) and a logout link. No topbar order badge (no #topbar-awaiting-badge element). The sidebar does NOT include: dashboard link, order management link, POS link, products/categories/inventory/reports/finance/settings/gcash/activity log links. The realtime_js block in base_kitchen.html loads: a <audio> element with id='kitchen-order-sound' pointing to {% static 'sounds/order_ready.mp3' %} (for new-preparing-order arrival notification) and <audio id='mark-ready-sound'> pointing to {% static 'sounds/new_order.mp3' %} (for confirmation when an order is marked ready). Does NOT load realtime.js (that drives the cashier TopbarOrderBadge — not relevant here). The kitchen page loads its own inline JS for the SSE connection (see step 4).

2. Create templates/kitchen/orders.html extending base_kitchen.html. Blocks: page_title='Kitchen Orders', body_attrs='data-kitchen-realtime="true"'. The page renders a responsive grid of order cards. Each card shows: order_number, customer_name, order type badge (Dine-In / Take-Out using existing .badge-dine-in/.badge-takeout or inline style), created_at formatted as time (e.g. 4:32 PM), order notes if non-empty (order.notes), and a list of order items (quantity × product_name, size label if size != 'none', item notes if non-empty). A 'MARK READY' button at the bottom of each card (POST to {% url 'kitchen:mark_ready' order.pk %}). Card uses existing .card CSS class. Order number displayed prominently. Does NOT show: subtotal, total, amount_paid, change, payment_method, gcash_* fields, is_paid, cashier name. If no orders: show an empty-state message ('No orders to prepare right now ✅'). Each card has a data-order-id attribute for JS targeting. The MARK READY button has class='btn btn-success mark-ready-btn' and data-order-id={{ order.pk }} data-url='{% url "kitchen:mark_ready" order.pk %}'.

3. Add CSS to templates/kitchen/orders.html (in extra_css block or as inline <style> in the template). Kitchen-specific styles: .kitchen-grid (CSS grid, repeat(auto-fill, minmax(300px, 1fr)), gap 16px). .kitchen-card (extends .card, adds left border 4px solid var(--caramel) for emphasis). .kitchen-card-header (order number + time row). .order-items-list (clean list, no bullets). .btn-mark-ready / .btn-success (if not already in main.css — use existing btn-primary style with green background overriding to #198754 if needed, or add .btn-success to main.css). .kitchen-empty-state (centered, muted, large emoji). New-order highlight animation: @keyframes slideInCard { from { opacity:0; transform:translateY(-12px); } to { opacity:1; transform:none; } } applied on .kitchen-card.new-arrival for 0.4s.

4. Add realtime SSE JavaScript to templates/kitchen/orders.html in the extra_js block. Use a self-contained inline <script> (not realtime.js, which is for cashier badge logic). The script:
   a. On DOMContentLoaded, connects to the kitchen SSE stream at window.KDM_URLS.kitchenStream (added in FEAT-002 step 8) via new EventSource(url).
   b. Listens for 'status_changed' events. When new_status == 'preparing': a new order arrived in the kitchen. Fetch the full order card HTML via a GET request to /kitchen/?order_id=<id>&partial=1 OR simply insert a placeholder card and reload — the simplest correct approach is: play kitchen-order-sound.play(), show a toast 'New order arrived: #<order_number>', then reload the page after 800ms (window.location.reload()). This avoids building a full client-side rendering pipeline while still giving realtime notification. When new_status == 'ready': the order was just marked ready (by this terminal or another). Remove the card with data-order-id matching the event's order_id from the DOM (card.remove()), play mark-ready-sound briefly, show toast '✅ Order #<order_number> is Ready'.
   c. Heartbeat events are ignored (no-op).
   d. On SSE error: log to console, browser auto-reconnects via EventSource API.
   e. The MARK READY button handler: on click, show loading state (button text → 'Marking...', disabled=true), POST via fetch to the mark_ready URL with CSRF token, on success remove the card from DOM + show toast, on error re-enable button + show error toast.
   f. Play sounds defensively (.play().catch(()=>{}) — autoplay policy).

5. Add server-side access enforcement review: audit every @cashier_or_admin_required and @admin_required decorated view in apps/orders/views.py, apps/dashboard/views.py, apps/finance/views.py, apps/inventory/views.py, apps/reports/views.py, apps/audit/views.py, apps/menu/views.py. These already block kitchen_staff because kitchen_staff is neither admin nor cashier. Verify that the cashier_or_admin_required decorator correctly blocks kitchen_staff (it checks is_admin_user OR is_cashier — kitchen_staff has neither, so it redirects to menu:index). No changes needed to existing decorators on existing views. Document this in FEAT findings.

6. Add tests in apps/kitchen/tests.py. Cover:
   - kitchen_orders view: 200 for kitchen_staff, 302-to-login for anonymous, redirect for cashier (wrong role), redirect for admin (wrong role — kitchen is kitchen_staff only)
   - mark_order_ready view: success for kitchen_staff + preparing order, 400 for already-ready order, 400 for non-preparing order (awaiting_payment), 302 for anonymous
   - Decorator tests: kitchen_staff_required blocks cashier, admin, anonymous; kitchen_or_admin_required allows admin but blocks cashier
   - Login redirect: kitchen_staff user → kitchen:orders
   Use Django's test client. Create test users with role='kitchen_staff' directly (CustomUser.objects.create_user(..., role='kitchen_staff')).
acceptance_criteria: templates/kitchen/orders.html renders without template errors and shows only orders with status='preparing'
Kitchen Staff sidebar shows only 'Kitchen Orders' link (no Dashboard, Order Management, POS, Products, Finance, etc.)
MARK READY button POSTs to mark_order_ready, card disappears from DOM on success
SSE connection on kitchen page uses /realtime/kitchen-stream/ (not /realtime/stream/)
New 'preparing' order triggers sound + toast + page reload on kitchen page
All new tests in apps/kitchen/tests.py pass
Existing tests in apps/accounts, apps/orders, apps/realtime all still pass
No financial data (total, is_paid, payment_method, gcash fields) appears in kitchen templates
verification: python manage.py test apps.kitchen  (all tests pass)
python manage.py test  (full test suite passes — no regressions)
python manage.py check  (no system check errors)
Manual: log in as kitchen_staff, confirm /kitchen/ loads, /dashboard/ redirects away, /orders/manage/ redirects away
